sermon.title: How to Have No Fail Success
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “How to Have No Fail Success,” Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the new covenant promises in Ezekiel 11, 36 and 37 — one heart, a new spirit, a heart of flesh, cleansing by the word, and the covenant of peace that makes believers priests — and shows where the New Testament says the same. He teaches that God says “I will” and does the changing, while we must respond, seek Him and apply ourselves. He closes with accounts of early martyrs and the deathbed words of well-known unbelievers.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes on references: at about 1:07 he gives the reference as “John 10:18” for “one fold and one shepherd”; those words are in John 10:16, so that passage is shown. At about 2:06 the captions read “17:2” for the prayer “Father, make them one”; those words are John 17:21, which is shown. At about 2:06 he says “in Acts one” for “on the day of Pentecost they were in one accord”; that description matches Acts 2:1, which is shown. At about 15:00 he reads Ezekiel 36:32 as “number 13” in his list, and at about 16:14 he reads Ezekiel 36:36 without naming the verse. The historical accounts of martyrs and of deathbed words are the speaker’s own and have not been checked by this site. Where he reads Scripture aloud his wording often differs slightly from the NKJV text shown with each section.

chunks.section_question: What is the new covenant promise in Ezekiel 11, and why should we know it?
chunks.short_answer: He says we should know the covenant, even have it memorized, because “this is powerful.” In Ezekiel 11 God says “I will gather you,” and he ties this to the church being the called-out ones, brought out of the power of Satan into a spiritual land, not a natural one.
chunks.text: So this is a very important thing. You got to know the covenant. You really do. You should have this memorized, basically. You need to pray about the covenant, you need to get this in your brain, because this is powerful. Okay, the new covenant, Ezekiel 11:16-21. First of all, He introduces the topic like Jeremiah does: “I will gather you from the people.” And in the New Testament we actually find that the church, the word church, means the called-out ones. Okay, and in Acts 26:18 the Bible says that Jesus came to turn people from darkness to light, from the power of Satan to the power of God. So He’s bringing us out from under the authority and the power, the kingdom of darkness and Satan, and placing us in, He isn’t bringing us into a natural land, He’s bringing us into a spiritual land. Got it?

chunks.section_question: What should we do to be changed, and do we have to wait for the rapture?
chunks.short_answer: He says not to try to do it on our own: “just relax in God,” seek Him, pray, read the word and go to church, and you will find yourself being changed. He gives Revelation 7:9, a great multitude from all nations before the throne, as the result, and says you don’t have to wait for the rapture: if you give God time, He will transform you into a priest who can minister to Him and to people. He says the apostles suffered greatly and did not turn from Jesus, and that if God did it for them, “He will do it for you.”

And see, He will do it. Who will do it? The “I will” will do it. We’re trying to do it on our own. Don’t do that. Just relax in God. Seek Him, pray, read the word, go to church, and you will find yourself being changed. You know as well as I do, when you first got saved, you weren’t much of a new creature. Hallelujah, it worked. How many want to be part of that process? You want to be part of that? [unclear]. Yeah. And how many of you know you can have it here on earth? We already learned that it’s nothing for Him to forgive us, but what you need is what? Deliverance. Absolutely. I just want to remind you that the apostles were stoned, beheaded, persecuted, crucified, tarred and feathered, exiled onto islands, driven out of communities they were in, in danger from bandits and elements,

chunks.section_question: What does he say about early Christian martyrs such as Polycarp and Perpetua?
chunks.short_answer: He tells of Polycarp, aged 86, who said he had served Jesus Christ 86 years, and of Perpetua, a young mother who refused to renounce Christ. He calls this “a powerful story that the new covenant works,” noting she was a new Christian. This passage contains a graphic account of her death.
chunks.text:
heard the gospel from John, was 86 years old when they were going to burn him at the stake, and his last words were, “86 years I’ve served Jesus Christ and He’s never done me the least wrong. How can I then blaspheme my King and my Savior?” Whoa. Amen. That’s power. Uh, he goes on to say, “We Christians are fixed in our minds not to change from good to evil, but for me it would be good to be changed from evil to good.” Isn’t he describing the Christian life? We’re in a process of being changed from evil to good, and here they’re going to kill him. Now this is the one I really like.

Perpetua was a wife and a mother. I can’t find her husband, but they said she was a wife and a mother of a nursing baby. She’s 22 years old, she just accepted Christ, and she’s going through catechism, she’s learning the basic scriptures over there in North Africa. And the governor, the government comes in and arrests them in the Bible study, and they told her if you denounce Christ you will live, and if you don’t you’re going to die. They took her baby from her. And how many, you know, for a woman who’s got a little baby, and the heart that a natural mother has for a baby, would be a big

temptation to renounce Christ. And she wouldn’t do it. So they came and took the baby from her. Her father came and tried to put a guilt trip on her: “What are you doing? Your baby needs you. Renounce Christ and live your life and take care of this baby.” She still would not budge. Now, folks, that new covenant is working, and she’s a baby Christian. She’s not been saved very long at all. So they take her to the arena when the governor was going to be there, put him on display. They stripped her naked and beat her before all the

people, and she would not give in at all. And then they put her in an area where there was a cow with rabies, a wild cow, and that cow just chased them and gored [unclear], and she’s wounded. And then the gladiators would come over and do the job, but the gladiator, when he came over, he was so taken by this woman standing for Christ, and she took his sword and put it up to her neck, and then the gladiator cut her throat and she died. Now, folks, that’s a powerful story that the new covenant works. Thomas Paine, on the other hand,

chunks.section_question: What does he say about the deathbed words of well-known unbelievers?
chunks.short_answer: After the martyrs, he says “on the other hand” and recounts what he says were the last words of several famous skeptics, who he says cried out in fear of hell. These are the speaker’s own historical accounts, not checked by this site.
chunks.text:
1809, the leading atheist writer in the American colonies, wrote the pamphlet Common Sense, which really stirred America to fight the Revolutionary War and become independent. On his deathbed, this is his words: “Stay with me, for God’s sake stay with me. I cannot bear to be left alone. Oh Lord, help me. Oh God, what have I done to suffer so much? What will become of me hereafter? I would give worlds, if I had them, that The Age of Reason had never been published.” That’s a book he published that put down Christianity. Now there’s some good things in that book. He brought out the ridiculous things in the church,

the things done in the church that we shouldn’t be doing, but he also ridiculed the church, God and Jesus in it. “The Age of Reason had never been published. Oh Lord, help me. Christ, help me.” Look at that word, Christ. He didn’t call on Allah. “No, don’t leave, stay with me. Send even a child to stay with me, for I’m on the edge of hell here alone. If ever the Devil had an agent, I have been that agent.” That’s his deathbed cry after reading The Age of Reason. faqs.question: What is the new covenant, according to this message?
faqs.answer: He walks through the promises in Ezekiel 11, 36 and 37 and says they are the new covenant: God gathers us, gives one heart, a new spirit, a heart of flesh, cleansing, and an everlasting covenant of peace.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “Although I have cast them far off among the Gentiles, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet I shall be a little sanctuary for them in the countries where they have gone.” ’ Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “I will gather you from the peoples, assemble you from the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.” ’ And they will go there, and they will take away all its detestable things and all its abominations from there. Then I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them, and take the stony heart out of their flesh, and give them a heart of flesh, that they may walk in My statutes and keep My judgments and do them; and they shall be My people, and I will be their God. But as for those whose hearts follow the desire for their detestable things and their abominations, I will recompense their deeds on their own heads,” says the Lord GOD.

faqs.question: What does the word “church” mean?
faqs.answer: He says the word church means the called-out ones, and ties it to Acts 26:18, where Jesus turns people from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God.

scriptures.text_nkjv: to open their eyes, in order to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.’

faqs.question: Can a pastor on earth be my pastor?
faqs.answer: He says no: he says we are “strictly delegated ministers of the gospel” and there is only one pastor, one shepherd, Jesus Christ.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And other sheep I have which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they will hear My voice; and there will be one flock and one shepherd.

faqs.question: What does Jesus pray about being one?
faqs.answer: He reads Jesus praying, “Father, make them one, that the world may believe and know that You have sent Me,” and says having one direction impresses the unbeliever.

scriptures.text_nkjv: that they all may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I in You; that they also may be one in Us, that the world may believe that You sent Me.

faqs.question: Does he connect John 3:16 and John 7:38?
faqs.answer: He says both promise something to whoever believes, eternal life in one and rivers of living water in the other, and that “they both come as a package.” He says John 7:38 speaks of the Holy Ghost, who would be in us.

scriptures.text_nkjv: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.”

faqs.question: Is there more to the Holy Ghost than receiving Christ?
faqs.answer: He says that when you accept Christ, He comes in you, but there is an infilling of the Holy Ghost of power, and they are two different things.

faqs.question: Why does he say we are not robots when we obey?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus gives us a heart to fall in love with Him, so we obey because we care, love and appreciate Him, not because of “thou shalt not.” He says His word also brings rewards.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word; and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.

faqs.question: Does God hold believers accountable for doing detestable things?
faqs.answer: He says that if you do the things God detests, He will come and hold you accountable, bringing problems and pain to correct you.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But as for those whose hearts follow the desire for their detestable things and their abominations, I will recompense their deeds on their own heads,” says the Lord GOD.

faqs.question: What does he mean by “God’s soap”?
faqs.answer: He means the word of God, which he says keeps washing and cleansing us. He points to Ephesians 5:26, the washing of the water by the word, and says we need to read it, study it and listen to Bible studies.

scriptures.text_nkjv: that He might sanctify and cleanse her with the washing of water by the word,

faqs.question: What does God promise about daily needs in Ezekiel 36?
faqs.answer: He says that in the verse about calling for the corn and laying no famine on them, God is saying He will bless your daily life, income, food, clothing and shelter.

scriptures.text_nkjv: I will deliver you from all your uncleannesses. I will call for the grain and multiply it, and bring no famine upon you.

faqs.question: What are the two sides of repentance?
faqs.answer: He says one is turning and the other is feeling sorry or bad for what you have done, and that we need both.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then you will remember your evil ways and your deeds that were not good; and you will loathe yourselves in your own sight, for your iniquities and your abominations.

faqs.question: Why does he say God blesses us?
faqs.answer: He says God’s ultimate goal is the unbeliever, and God blesses us so He can reach our neighbors, parents and other people.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then the nations which are left all around you shall know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt the ruined places and planted what was desolate. I, the LORD, have spoken it, and I will do it.”

faqs.question: What could priests do under the covenant of peace?
faqs.answer: He says they had authority to come into the very presence of God and minister to God, and to minister to the people, and could go in and talk to God directly.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore say, ‘Behold, I give to him My covenant of peace;

faqs.question: Who does the changing: God or me?
faqs.answer: He says “the ‘I will’ will do it” and not to try to do it on our own, but also, near the end, that we have to put some effort into it.

faqs.question: Can I have these promises here on earth?
faqs.answer: He says you don’t have to wait for the rapture. If you give God time, he says, He will transform you into a priest who can minister to Him and to people and possess His promises.
